rule: Paint every background cell that touches the figure only diagonally (a diagonal neighbour is a figure cell and no orthogonal neighbour is) with the inner colour, i.e. the figure colour with the strictly smallest bounding box.
scope: Paint background cells with diagonal but no orthogonal figure contact using the unique smallest-bounding-box colour. Random canvases 10..30, figure boxes 4..28 subject to a one-cell margin, two figure colours and four symmetry modes. Exact figure dimensions, symmetry and inner-colour overrides are supported; default background remains 7.

authored_scope: Supported: grid sizes 10..20 per side, figure boxes 4..10 per side with a 1-cell margin, two figure colours (outer and inner) sampled from the non-background colours, four symmetry modes (quad, left/right, up/down, none), and variable density of outer and inner cells, including inner cells mixed with outer cells. Not supported: three or more figure colours, a background other than 7 in random samples, multiple separate figures, and figures that touch the grid edge.
authored_constraints: Background is 7 and is the majority colour.
The outer colour touches all four edges of the figure box, so its bounding box is the whole figure box.
Inner colour cells lie inside a strictly smaller interior box, so the inner bounding box is strictly smaller and there are no ties.
Both figure colours are present, distinct and differ from the background.
The figure keeps at least a one-cell margin from the grid border, so the whole new ring fits.
The output differs from the input.
